samples.sample_label: 0.04Nb steel aged at 773 K for 3 h

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Ingot prepared by induction melting in a water-cooled copper crucible, then re-melted and swiftly poured into a rotating copper mold to obtain steel strips (60 × 70 × 2.5 mm) through near-rapid solidification.
Aging treatment performed on a portion of the as-cast steel strips in a tubular vacuum furnace at 773 K for 3 h.

structures.overall_structure: Duplex ferrite + austenite microstructure: irregular-shaped ferrite randomly dispersed within the austenite matrix, with submicron NbC particles and nano-scale intragranular κ-carbides in the austenite.

phases_present.grain_size: 9 μm (as-cast 0.04Nb value; austenite grain size remains almost unchanged after aging)

phases_present.morphology: irregular-shaped islands randomly dispersed in austenite matrix

precipitates.distribution: Submicron white NbC particles dispersed within the austenite matrix; average size and volume fraction increase slightly with higher aging temperature and more Nb content.
Dense nano-scale intragranular κ-carbides dispersed in austenite; content and size increase with aging temperature, but 0.04Nb steel consistently has smaller content and size than 0.02Nb steel.

defect_interactions.interaction_type: NbC particle pinning of austenite grain boundaries
defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: Intergranular NbC particles hinder austenite grain-boundary motion and grain growth, refining the austenite grain size in the 0.04Nb steel.

interfaces.phase_evolution: Aging at 773 K for 3 h does not measurably change the ferrite/austenite phase constitution, but promotes growth of NbC and κ-carbides.

measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: gauge width 4 mm, gauge length 12 mm
measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Tensile tests on MTS Criterion 44 universal testing machine; at least four repetitions per steel strip. Vickers microhardness (MH-5L) with indentation load 200 gf and holding time 20 s.

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: Yield strength of 0.04Nb steels exceeds that of 0.02Nb steels by ≈71 MPa; 0.04Nb steels generally exhibit slightly higher strength and poorer plasticity than 0.02Nb steels.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: D/max-2500 instrument at 40 kV, scanning 30°–100° at 4°/min
characterization_methods.purpose: Phase identification and XRD line-profile analysis
characterization_methods.key_findings: The 0.04Nb steel consists of ferrite and austenite; peak intensity shows almost no significant change after aging.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Apollo 300 thermal field emission SEM equipped with EBSD detector; EBSD step size 300 nm; samples electropolished with 10 vol% perchloric acid alcohol solution at 25 V for 10 s
characterization_methods.purpose: Microstructure characterization and ferrite content measurement (ImageJ)
characterization_methods.key_findings: Irregular-shaped ferrite randomly dispersed in austenite matrix; ferrite content 18.4 vol% at 773 K/3 h; submicron white NbC particles present.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: JEOL JEM-2100 TEM operating at 200 kV; TEM specimens prepared by double-jet electropolishing with 10% perchloric acid + 90% alcohol at ≈30 °C and 35 V
characterization_methods.purpose: Nano-scale precipitate characterization (NbC and intragranular κ-carbides)
characterization_methods.key_findings: Submicron white particles identified as NbC; nano-scale intragranular κ-carbides dispersed in austenite and coherent with austenite ([100]γ // [100]κ).

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Vickers hardness tester (MH-5L), indentation load 200 gf, holding time 20 s
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: indentation load 200 gf; holding time 20 s
characterization_methods.key_findings: Microhardness of 0.04Nb steel aged at 773 K/3 h is 465 HV.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: ambient temperature; strain rate 2.5 × 10^-4 s^-1; gauge width 4 mm; gauge length 12 mm; minimum four repetitions
characterization_methods.key_findings: YS 1014 ± 16 MPa, UTS 1122 ± 14 MPa, total elongation 14 ± 2 % for 0.04Nb steel aged at 773 K/3 h.

computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Nb content has limited impact on the liquid-to-solid transformation temperature, leading to similar constituent phase content in the 0.02Nb and 0.04Nb steels.

computational_details.simulation_method: Diffusion coefficient calculation (Al and C in austenite)
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Nb presence slightly decreases C diffusion in austenite (strong Nb–C affinity) and slightly increases Al diffusion; slower C diffusion decelerates κ-carbide nucleation and growth.

computational_details.potential_model_or_database: PAW potentials; U = 2.59 eV for Fe; plane-wave cutoff 500 eV; Gaussian smearing 0.05 eV; convergence < 0.03 eV Å^-1; vacuum 15 Å; 6 × 6 × 6 Monkhorst–Pack k-points
computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: 2 × 2 × 2 supercell of κ-carbide (Fe3AlC, E21); Nb substitution at Fe face-centered site (Fe23NbAl8C8) and Al corner site (Fe24Al7NbC8)
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Nb doping significantly increases κ-carbide formation energy, explaining the reduced κ-carbide content and size in 0.04Nb steel.

analytical_models.model_name: Formation energy equation E_F = E_DFT − Σ N_X μ_X
analytical_models.model_note: Doping κ-carbide with Nb significantly increases its formation energy.

computational_details.simulation_method: Analytical strengthening-mechanism calculation for austenite and ferrite
computational_details.boundary_and_initial_conditions: Parameters: austenite M = 3.06, α = 0.23, b = 0.26 nm, G = 70 GPa; Hall–Petch coefficient k_γ = 14.55 MPa·mm^-1/2; κ-carbide shearing N = 6, γ_APB = 350 mJ/m^-2; ferrite M_F = 2, α_F = 0.4, G_F = 76 GPa.
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Calculated contributions explain the higher yield strength of the 0.04Nb steel.

analytical_models.model_name: Dislocation strengthening (Taylor): σ_d = M α G b √ρ
analytical_models.model_note: For 0.04Nb steel aged at 773 K for 3 h.

analytical_models.model_name: Grain boundary strengthening (Hall–Petch): σ_g = k_γ d^-1/2
analytical_models.model_note: For 0.04Nb steel aged at 773 K for 3 h.

unmapped_findings: As-cast 0.04Nb steel austenite composition (EPMA/Table 4): Mn 13.03, Al 8.37, Cr 3.97, C 1.33, Nb 0.038, Fe 64.07 wt% (alloy-level, as-cast information relevant to the 0.04Nb alloy).
EPMA shows Nb uniformly dispersed within austenite grains of as-cast 0.04Nb steel, with only sporadic Nb enrichment at grain boundaries.

Nb addition raises the MC (NbC) precipitation temperature from ≈973 K (0 Nb) to 1573 K (0.05 wt% Nb), enabling NbC particles to pin austenite grain boundaries during the δ-ferrite → γ-austenite transformation.
The austenite grain size of 0.04Nb steels is approximately half that of 0.02Nb steels due to precipitation of NbC particles.
No coarsened intergranular κ-carbides were detected in 0.04Nb steel after aging treatment at 723–823 K (which includes the 773 K/3 h state).

The paper notes that for Nb-containing steels aged at temperatures exceeding 773 K, κ-carbide precipitation was the principal strengthening factor (statement may or may not include the 773 K/3 h state; text is ambiguous about the threshold).
